an3.1:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
an3.1:1.3: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
an3.1:2.1: “Bhikkhus, whatever perils arise all arise on account of the fool, not on account of the wise person.
an3.1:2.2: Whatever calamities arise all arise on account of the fool, not on account of the wise person.
an3.1:2.3: Whatever misfortunes arise all arise on account of the fool, not on account of the wise person.
an3.1:2.4: Just as a fire that starts in a house made of reeds or grass burns down even a house with a peaked roof, plastered inside and out, draft-free, with bolts fastened and shutters closed;
an3.1:2.6: all arise on account of the fool, not on account of the wise person. (1) Thus, bhikkhus, the fool brings peril, the wise person brings no peril; (2) the fool brings calamity, the wise person brings no calamity;
an3.1:3.2: the wise person brings no misfortune.
an3.1:3.4: There is no peril from the wise person; there is no calamity from the wise person; there is no misfortune from the wise person.
an3.1:4.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus:
an3.1:4.2: ‘We will avoid the three qualities possessing which one is known as a fool, and we will undertake and practice the three qualities possessing which one is known as a wise person.’
an3.1:4.3: It is in this way that you should train yourselves.”
